# Environment reference

<!-- Generated from config/environment.reference by scripts/generate-environment-reference.ts. Do not edit. -->

Every environment variable the Marina server and its world definitions read, generated from [`config/environment.reference`](../../config/environment.reference). Everything is optional; with no configuration a loopback `bun run start` runs the ungated `local` trust profile. For a short starter, copy [`.env.example`](../../.env.example) to `.env`.

Values are defaults or safe examples. Flags: **secret** values are never displayed; **protected** keys are never written by the dashboard (edit `.env` or the process environment); **restart** keys are read once at startup; **internal** keys are set by Marina itself or read only by a command-line client, and are hidden from Admin → Settings.

Script, test and CI knobs are in [docs/guides/testing.md](../guides/testing.md) and [docs/guides/release-qualification.md](../guides/release-qualification.md); SDK example knobs in [`src/sdk/examples/.env.example`](../../src/sdk/examples/.env.example); memory-service example knobs in [`examples/memory-service/.env.example`](../../examples/memory-service/.env.example).

## Network and ports

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `WS_PORT=3300` | WebSocket, web chat, dashboard and HTTP API port (the OpenAI- and Ollama-compatible /v1 and /api routes are served here too). 0 picks a free port for the listener, but internal agents and benchmark runs still dial 3300, so use a real port when agents run. | restart |
| `WS_HOST=127.0.0.1` | Bind address for the WebSocket/HTTP and MCP listeners; the default is loopback only. Unless MARINA_ALLOW_INSECURE_PUBLIC=true, a non-loopback bind is fatal at startup when login is passwordless (MARINA_AUTH off, which also covers MARINA_AUTONOMY=open), when MARINA_OPEN_API=true, or under MARINA_PROFILE=local. | protected, restart |
| `MARINA_HOST=127.0.0.1` | Deprecated alias of WS_HOST (WS_HOST wins when both are set). | protected, restart |
| `MARINA_PUBLIC=false` | true binds 0.0.0.0 without naming an interface. An explicit WS_HOST wins. | protected, restart |
| `MARINA_ALLOW_INSECURE_PUBLIC=false` | Acknowledge an unauthenticated non-loopback bind (see WS_HOST). Only for a network you control; prefer MARINA_AUTH=better-auth. | protected, restart |
| `TELNET_PORT=0` | Telnet port. 0 (the default) is off. Telnet is plaintext and unauthenticated, and telnet sessions can never run host commands. | restart |
| `MCP_PORT=3301` | MCP (Model Context Protocol) port. Default: the bound WebSocket port + 1 (also with WS_PORT=0). 0 disables. | restart |
| `LOG_PORT=3302` | Real-time log viewer port. Default: the bound WebSocket port + 2 (also with WS_PORT=0). 0 disables. | restart |
| `WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_IP=100` | Maximum concurrent WebSocket connections per client IP. | restart |
| `MARINA_TRUST_PROXY=false` | Trust X-Forwarded-For when resolving the client IP for every per-IP rate limiter. Enable only behind a trusted reverse proxy. | protected |
| `NODE_ENV=production`<br>`REVERSE_PROXY=1`<br>`HTTPS_PROXY=` | When NODE_ENV=production and neither HTTPS_PROXY nor REVERSE_PROXY is set, Marina logs a hint that no TLS proxy was detected. Only presence matters. Bun's fetch also honours HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY and NO_PROXY for outbound requests. | restart |
| `MARINA_NAME=Marina` | Human-readable instance name. Shown in the dashboard and stamped as the origin on federation and provenance records. Defaults to the world name. | restart |

## API authentication and access

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MODEL_API_KEYS=sk-marina-change-me` | Comma-separated bearer tokens accepted on /v1, the Ollama-compatible /api routes and MCP. Under the local profile Marina also generates a key into &lt;DB_PATH&gt;.local-api-key (mode 600) and prints it at boot, so local clients need nothing here. | secret |
| `MEM_API_KEYS=sk-agent-1:scout` | Comma-separated secret:agent pairs for the /mem REST API and /api/probe. Unset keeps /mem closed, except with MARINA_OPEN_API=true or, under the local profile, the local model-API key plus an X-Agent-Name header. | secret |
| `MARINA_KEY_SECRET=` | Encrypts provider keys stored through Admin → Keys (AES-256-GCM, 16+ characters; generate with `openssl rand -base64 32`). Unset: Marina generates one in &lt;DB_PATH&gt;.key-secret (0600) and encrypts keys saved from then on; existing plaintext rows keep working, and an explicit value also migrates them. Back the secret (or that file) up with the database: changing or losing it orphans stored keys, which must then be re-entered. Environment provider keys are never stored. | secret, protected, restart |
| `MARINA_OPEN_API=false` | Development only: accept unauthenticated requests on the model, memory and dashboard read APIs. It does not grant operator actions: key and settings management, spawning and deletion still need an operator, and writes are refused outside the local profile. Fatal with a non-loopback bind unless MARINA_ALLOW_INSECURE_PUBLIC=true. | protected |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173` | Comma-separated origins allowed for CORS. Unset sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (same-origin only). |  |
| `MARINA_DASHBOARD_CSP=` | Content-Security-Policy for the dashboard HTML. Unset uses the built-in policy; `off` drops the header; any other value replaces the policy verbatim. | protected |

|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_AUTH=better-auth` | `better-auth` requires human sign-in on the web chat and dashboard (email/password plus any configured OAuth providers) and rejects passwordless name login. A signed-in identity is bridged to a named Marina entity. Agents keep authenticating with session tokens. Off by default. | protected, restart |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=` | Required with MARINA_AUTH=better-auth: 32+ characters (generate with `openssl rand -base64 32`; `bun run init --preset shared-team` writes one). | secret, protected, restart |

| `BETTER_AUTH_DB_PATH=marina-auth.db` | SQLite file for the auth tables, kept separate from the world database. | restart |
| `MARINA_AUTH_ADMIN_EMAILS=you@example.com` | Comma-separated verified email addresses promoted to admin when sign-in is on. Replaces MARINA_ADMINS under MARINA_AUTH. | protected |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=` | OAuth sign-in providers. Set both the id and the secret to enable each one. | restart |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=` | OAuth sign-in providers. Set both the id and the secret to enable each one. | secret, restart |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=` | OAuth sign-in providers. Set both the id and the secret to enable each one. | restart |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=` | OAuth sign-in providers. Set both the id and the secret to enable each one. | secret, restart |
| `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID=` | OAuth sign-in providers. Set both the id and the secret to enable each one. | restart |
| `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET=` | OAuth sign-in providers. Set both the id and the secret to enable each one. | secret, restart |

## Trust profile, autonomy and admins

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_PROFILE=local` | Who this Marina is for. Derived when unset: `local` when every listener binds loopback and MARINA_AUTH is off, `shared` when MARINA_AUTH=better-auth, `public` for any non-loopback bind. `local` is ungated: all safety gates pass, loopback logins are sovereign, rate limits, login caps and memory admission budgets are off, and database durability defaults to `normal`; audit (exec decisions, cognitive ledger, memory receipts, trust labels) stays on. `shared` enforces gates, ranks and limits with sign-in identifying people; `public` enforces everything. `local` with a non-loopback bind is fatal unless MARINA_ALLOW_INSECURE_PUBLIC=true. | protected, restart |
| `MARINA_AUTONOMY=guarded` | Autonomy posture, env-only by design. `guarded`: supervised gate attempts need a witness window. `earned`: agents with enough standing run supervised operations and a witness attests afterwards. `open`: every gate passes except the destructive core (key.manage, admin.destructive, shell.exec, code.exec.unrestricted, world.code); `open` does pass code.exec. Unset means `guarded`, except under the local profile, where unset is ungated and only an explicit `guarded` brings the gates back. `open` with a non-loopback bind and passwordless login is fatal. | protected, restart |
| `MARINA_ADMINS=YourName` | Comma-separated entity names promoted to sovereign on login, honoured only for loopback or in-process connections and ignored under MARINA_AUTH. Redundant under the local profile, where loopback logins are already sovereign. | protected |
| `MARINA_MAX_LOGINS=0` | Instance-wide cap on concurrent entity logins. 0 is unlimited. Internal room and crew agents are exempt (MAX_AGENTS caps them). Not enforced under the local profile. |  |
| `MARINA_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS_PER_MIN=10` | Login and reconnect attempts per minute per client IP (MCP sessions share their peer's bucket). 0 disables. | restart |
| `MARINA_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS=604800000` | Absolute lifetime of a session token in milliseconds (default 7 days). Activity refreshes the 24-hour idle window only up to this cap; a reconnect mints a new session. |  |

## Challenges and agent lineage

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_CHALLENGES=on` | When a caller is refused by a rank floor or safety gate, Marina asks its creator and the admins with a token instead of only refusing; `challenge approve <token> [once\|always]` re-runs the held command. `off` restores plain refusals. |  |
| `MARINA_CHALLENGE_TTL_MS=3600000` | How long an unanswered challenge stays open, in milliseconds. |  |
| `MARINA_CHALLENGE_JUDGE=off` | Challenge judge (needs a MARINA_DECISIONS backend). `observe` scores held commands in shadow. `on` also auto-approves `once` for a gate only after it earned that gate (25+ approved calls at 85% or better, 95% lower bound), never for the core gates, never `always`, never a deny. `challenge stats` shows the record. | protected |
| `MARINA_MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH=3` | Deepest spawn lineage an agent may extend (lead → sub-lead → specialist). |  |
| `MARINA_STANDING_PER_SPAWNED_CHILD=25` | Standing per concurrent child an earned spawner may keep alive (budget = floor(standing / this), capped by MAX_AGENTS). |  |
| `MARINA_MAX_REPLICAS_PER_RUN=5` | Total copies `evolve replicate` may seed from one accepted run. |  |
| `MARINA_EVOLVE_TRIALS=` | `here` lets a dedicated parallel world run `evolve trial` itself. Trials otherwise run only in a World Collective child. Never set it on a world you care about. | protected |
| `STANDING_HALF_LIFE_DAYS=60` | Standing decay half-life in days (minimum 1; a non-numeric value falls back to 60). Shorter means rank derived from standing demotes faster. | restart |

## World

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_WORLD=default` | World definition to load: the file name of any module in worlds/ (default, showcase, commons, research, evolve, empty, …). | restart |
| `START_ROOM=` | Room where new players spawn. Defaults to the world's start room. | restart |
| `TICK_MS=1000` | Engine tick interval in milliseconds. | restart |
| `MARINA_COMMAND_PHASE_BUDGET_MS=150` | Wall-clock budget for the per-tick command phase, in milliseconds. | restart |
| `MARINA_MACRO_MAX_DEPTH=8`<br>`MARINA_MACRO_MAX_EXPANSIONS=100` | Macro expansion limits: nesting depth (a macro that runs a macro …) and commands one top-level macro invocation may expand to. 0 is unlimited. Unset, the shared/public defaults are 8 and 100, and the local-ungated profile or MARINA_AUTONOMY=open is unlimited. A macro cycle is always refused, and every expanded command still costs one rate-limit token. |  |
| `MARINA_ROOM_AGENTS=true` | `false` suppresses every room-agent auto-spawn (the LLM agents rooms start on first entry). Any other value leaves it on. Room agents need a provider key. |  |
| `MARINA_WORKBENCH_MODEL=openai/gpt-6-luna` | Model for the default Workbench's Host, Builder, Critic and Chronicler. Unset tries MARINA_CREW_MODEL, then openai/gpt-6-luna (OPENAI_API_KEY), openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna (OPENROUTER_API_KEY), huggingface/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY or HF_TOKEN), then marina/default. | restart |
| `MARINA_CREW_MODEL=marina/default` | Shared crew-model override for the Workbench, Showcase and focused single-outcome worlds. | restart |
| `MARINA_ANSWERER_COUNT=4`<br>`MARINA_ANSWERER_MODEL=`<br>`MARINA_MATH_MODEL=`<br>`MARINA_REFLECTOR_MODEL=` | Showcase world only: size of the answerer crew and per-crew model overrides (each falls back to MARINA_CREW_MODEL). | restart |
| `MARINA_AGENT_MODELS=Answerer=openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5.5,Translator=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` | Per-agent model map for boot-seeded agents, any world: comma list of Name=model (names case-insensitive; the model string passes through as-is). Wins over the per-role variables above and MARINA_CREW_MODEL. Applied on every boot to agents the seed still owns — a user-customized or retired agent is never touched — exactly like the per-role variables. A name matching no seeded agent, or a malformed entry, is logged as a warning at boot. | restart |
| `MARINA_ENDPOINTS=council,debate,decompose` | Showcase world only: which autonomous coordinators to seed beyond marina:answerer (comma list of council, debate, decompose; empty or `none` seeds none). Unset seeds all three. Each is a loop that spends tokens even when its endpoint is never called. | restart |
| `MARINA_SEED_SKILLS=false` | Showcase world only: `true` seeds the universal skill packages. | restart |
| `MARINA_MODEL_FAST_PATH=true` | `false` disables the verified-arithmetic fast path on marina:answerer (simple arithmetic otherwise returns without a crew round). |  |
| `MARINA_ASK_MODEL=true` | `false` turns off model synthesis in `ask` and `dig` (retrieval only) and the model interpretation pass in `desire`. Any other value keeps them on. |  |
| `MARINA_EVOLUTION_PROTOCOLS=false` | `true` enables native evolution protocols: passive experiment lineage and evidence analysis over the experiment command. Nothing is auto-run or auto-promoted. |  |
| `MARINA_UNIFIED_CANVAS=false` | `true` makes the retired Unified Canvas (ReactFlow world graph) reachable at /?unified. |  |

## Model provider keys

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=` | Anthropic API key. Set one provider key for agents that think; OPENROUTER_API_KEY is the most versatile because `forecast` and the arena research path also need it. Environment keys and keys added in Admin → Keys both work on every path; the environment wins and survives database resets. | secret |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY=` | OpenAI API key. | secret |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY=`<br>`GOOGLE_API_KEY=` | Google Gemini API key (GOOGLE_API_KEY is accepted as an alias). | secret |
| `GROQ_API_KEY=` | Groq API key. | secret |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=` | OpenRouter API key. Also required by the `forecast` command and POST /v1/forecast. | secret |
| `HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY=`<br>`HF_TOKEN=` | Hugging Face Inference Providers key (router.huggingface.co). Address models as `huggingface/<org>/<model>`, optionally suffixed `:fastest`, `:cheapest` or `:<provider>`. HF_TOKEN is accepted as well. | secret |
| `CEREBRAS_API_KEY=`<br>`XAI_API_KEY=`<br>`MISTRAL_API_KEY=`<br>`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=` | More OpenAI-compatible providers. Each is also an upstream for marina/default (defaults: gpt-oss-120b, deepseek-flash, mistral-small-latest, grok-4.7; override with MARINA_DEFAULT_&lt;PROVIDER&gt;_MODEL). | secret |

## Local model runtimes

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `LLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/v1` | llama.cpp server (OpenAI-compatible). Setting the base URL or the key opts in; llama is then the first marina/default fallback. Address models as `llama/<id>`. The key is only needed when the server runs with --api-key. | restart |
| `LLAMA_API_KEY=` | llama.cpp server (OpenAI-compatible). Setting the base URL or the key opts in; llama is then the first marina/default fallback. Address models as `llama/<id>`. The key is only needed when the server runs with --api-key. | secret, restart |
| `OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1` | Ollama (OpenAI-compatible, usually keyless). Setting the base URL or the key opts in as a marina/default fallback after llama. Address models as `ollama/<id>`. | restart |
| `OLLAMA_API_KEY=` | Ollama (OpenAI-compatible, usually keyless). Setting the base URL or the key opts in as a marina/default fallback after llama. Address models as `ollama/<id>`. | secret, restart |
| `VIBETHINKER_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1` | VibeThinker served by vLLM or SGLang. Usable only as an explicit `vibethinker/<id>` model, never as a marina/default fallback. In Docker it is the optional `vibethinker` compose profile, whose own VIBETHINKER_MODEL, VIBETHINKER_CTX and VIBETHINKER_MODELS_DIR are read by docker-compose.yml, not by Marina. | restart |
| `VIBETHINKER_API_KEY=` | VibeThinker served by vLLM or SGLang. Usable only as an explicit `vibethinker/<id>` model, never as a marina/default fallback. In Docker it is the optional `vibethinker` compose profile, whose own VIBETHINKER_MODEL, VIBETHINKER_CTX and VIBETHINKER_MODELS_DIR are read by docker-compose.yml, not by Marina. | secret, restart |
| `LLAMA_CONTEXT_WINDOW=16384`<br>`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_WINDOW=8192`<br>`VIBETHINKER_CONTEXT_WINDOW=` | Pin the context window (tokens) the agent compactor budgets against. Normally autodetected at launch (llama.cpp /props, Ollama /api/show); these win over the probe. Without either, llama uses 16384, Ollama 8192 and VibeThinker 40960. | restart |
| `MARINA_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW=128000` | Context window assumed for marina/default. Set it when marina/default proxies to a small local model, or requests overflow it. |  |
| `MARINA_LOCAL_OUTPUT_FRACTION=0.25` | Share of a local model's context window reserved for output (0 &lt; f ≤ 0.5; higher values are clamped). It scales with the configured window, so pin a real window above for large local servers. |  |
| `MARINA_LOCAL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=32768` | Optional hard cap in tokens on local-model output. Unset applies the fraction alone. |  |
| `MARINA_TOKEN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN=3` | Characters per token in the compactor's prompt-size estimate. Lower compacts earlier; raising it risks oversized prompts the upstream rejects. |  |
| `MARINA_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_TOKENS=2000` | Tool-result text block cap. Unset: max(2000, 15% of the effective prompt window), recalculated after model changes and overflow recovery. A positive integer sets a fixed cap. Truncation is labeled; originals are archived before compaction. Prefer narrower retrievals when a result exceeds the cap. |  |

## Default and fallback models

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_DEFAULT_MODEL=marina/default` | Model for agents spawned without one, and the fallback for unrecognized models. marina/default calls this instance's own /v1, which routes to whichever provider has a key. A default model set at runtime (dashboard or `admin`) wins. |  |
| `MARINA_DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5`<br>`MARINA_DEFAULT_OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-6-luna`<br>`MARINA_DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-3.1-flash-lite`<br>`MARINA_DEFAULT_OPENROUTER_MODEL=openai/gpt-6-luna`<br>`MARINA_DEFAULT_GROQ_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-120b`<br>`MARINA_DEFAULT_HUGGINGFACE_MODEL=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`<br>`MARINA_DEFAULT_LLAMA_MODEL=local-model` | Model /v1 uses on each provider when it proxies directly upstream (no model agent is online for the requested channel). The variable name is MARINA_DEFAULT_&lt;PROVIDER&gt;_MODEL. |  |
| `MARINA_DEFAULT_OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen3:4b` | Ollama default: the first model in Ollama's /api/tags (read at boot), else qwen3:4b. |  |
| `MODEL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=600000` | Upstream timeout for /v1 requests in milliseconds. Non-streaming client connections also close at Bun's 255-second idle limit. |  |
| `MODEL_REQUEST_REMINDERS=1` | `0` stops re-posting an unanswered routed model_request as a reminder at 25% and 60% of the timeout. |  |
| `MARINA_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS=16384` | Output-token cap marina/default sends upstream per completion (also the compactor's output reservation). Extended thinking on this path is clamped to this value minus 1024. |  |

## Agent runtime

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENT_AUTORESPAWN=false` | Restart saved agents at boot, including world-seeded ones such as the Workbench population and the Chronicler. Unset: on for a local install (local profile) with a usable provider, off otherwise; `true`/`false` overrides. `readiness` shows what is live. | restart |
| `MAX_AGENTS=30` | Maximum concurrently running agents. | restart |
| `MAX_AGENT_UPTIME_MS=86400000` | Maximum agent uptime in milliseconds before the runtime stops it (default 24 hours). | restart |
| `MARINA_DISABLED_AGENTS=` | Comma-separated agent names that seeders, autorespawn and room-agent spawning must not bring back. `agent disable <name>` does the same in-world and persists. |  |
| `MARINA_TASK_LEASE_MS=900000` | Renewable lease on a newly claimed task, in milliseconds. Workers renew with `task heartbeat <id>`; expired ordinary work reopens. |  |
| `AGENT_CREW_MAX_TOKENS=2048` | Output-token cap for request-driven (crew) agents. Unset: 2048 with thinking off; with thinking enabled, pi-ai's thinking budget + 2048 answer/tool tokens, bounded by the provider output limit and half the context window. An explicit insufficient cap is honored with a warning; reasoning depth may be reduced. |  |
| `AGENT_COMPACT_MAX_TOKENS=4096` | Output-token cap for cloud agents using the compact tool profile. Unset: 4096 with thinking off; with thinking enabled, pi-ai's thinking budget + 2048 answer/tool tokens, bounded by the provider output limit and half the context window. An explicit insufficient cap is honored with a warning. |  |
| `AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_RUN=16` | Tool calls one agent run may make before it yields. Unset: 8 for crew responders, 16 for autonomous agents. A value applies to both. |  |
| `MARINA_MAX_TURNS_PER_PROMPT=24` | Model calls one prompt may take before the loop yields to the next cycle. |  |
| `MARINA_CHANNEL_SENDS_PER_RUN=3` | Ceiling on public channel sends per agent run. Each agent's own budget defaults to 1 and may be set up to this ceiling with `memory set channel_sends <n>`; 0 disables agent channel sends. Tells are never capped. |  |
| `AGENT_IDLE_TICK_MS=60000`<br>`AGENT_ACTIVE_TICK_MS=15000` | Quiet-cycle and active-cycle intervals for autonomous agents, in milliseconds. Defaults: idle max(60000, 5 × cycle delay); active max(15000, cycle delay). |  |
| `AGENT_CHANNEL_REPLY_COOLDOWN_MS=30000` | Minimum gap between an agent's replies on one channel, in milliseconds. |  |
| `MARINA_AGENT_THINKING=off` | Default extended-thinking level for spawned agents: off, minimal, low, medium, high or xhigh. `agent spawn … thinking:<level>` wins; crew responders stay off unless set explicitly. |  |
| `MARINA_TOOL_EXECUTION=auto` | Multi-tool turn execution. `auto` runs batches containing a world-mutating tool in order and fans read-only batches out; `parallel` and `sequential` apply to every batch. |  |
| `MARINA_DEFERRED_TOOLS=on` | `off` keeps every typed tool schema resident in the `full` tool profile. On by default: the core set is resident and other tools load by name through `marina_tool_search`. |  |
| `MARINA_AGENT_PROMPT_CACHE=on` | `off` stops agents' marina/* requests carrying prompt-cache markers and a per-agent session id. On by default; Marina's proxy strips the markers for upstreams that reject them. |  |
| `MARINA_STRICT_TOOLS=on` | `off` sends tools without `strict: true`. On by default for closed, all-required schemas; upstreams that do not implement strict mode ignore it. |  |
| `MARINA_OPENROUTER_REQUIRE_PARAMETERS=on` | `off` stops asking OpenRouter for `provider.require_parameters` on agent requests that carry tools. On by default, so a request is never served by a provider that ignores `tools`; dropped per model when no endpoint supports every parameter. |  |
| `MARINA_OPENROUTER_REASONING_OFF=on` | `off` never sends `reasoning: {enabled: false}` to OpenRouter. By default an agent with thinking off sends it only for a model whose spawn-time tool probe still made a tool call without reasoning; a model that says reasoning is mandatory stops receiving it. |  |
| `MARINA_TOOL_PROBE=warn` | Spawn-time tool-calling probe for an unlisted model id or any OpenRouter model: `warn` reports a model that answered without a tool call (readiness, `agent status`), `refuse` also stops a crew lead on it, `off` skips the probe. Default `warn` (`off` under a test runner). |  |
| `MARINA_OUTPUT_REPAIR=on` | Output repair when a model's output misses its required shape (prose where a reply or tool call was owed, malformed JSON or arguments): `on` = deterministic parse, then one re-encoding shot whose values must appear verbatim in the original; `parse` = deterministic only; `off` = raw output. Repaired deliveries carry `repaired:parse` / `repaired:shot`. |  |
| `MARINA_REPAIR_MODEL=openrouter/google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | Model for server-side repair shots (`marina/verify` final output); must be a reachable upstream id. Default: the model whose output is repaired. Agents and forecast runs repair with their own model. |  |
| `MARINA_SYSTEM_TOOLS_PROSE=on` | `off` omits the tools prose section from the lean agent system prompt. |  |
| `MARINA_CONTINUATION_BUDGET_BYTES=6000` | Byte allowance for per-cycle context. Unset: effective prompt tokens / 8, clamped to 6000–16000 bytes. Automatic memory gets 2048–4096 content bytes. A fixed override has a minimum of 1000; mandatory sections can exceed it. Optional sections are deferred and remain eligible on the next scheduled cycle. |  |
| `MARINA_PERCEPTION_MODEL_REQUEST_MAX_CHARS=2000` | Clamp in characters for a model_request perception line (minimum 400). Its content is the caller's question. Other addressed requests and JSON results get 1200 chars; ambient chatter gets 400. |  |
| `MARINA_FORCED_ACTION_NUDGE=all` | What forces a tool call after a silent turn. `all` (default): any addressed or high-priority event. `requests`: only an event that owes a reply — a request tell, an addressed post whose body is a request, or a request already in the reply ledger; addressed information still wakes the agent but is not tracked as owed or nudged. |  |
| `MARINA_AGENT_CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS=48000`<br>`MARINA_AGENT_CONTEXT_TARGET_TOKENS=16000` | Absolute cap on an agent's conversation, in estimated tokens (system prompt and tool schemas excluded). Default 48000; `0`/`off` disables it (compaction then fires only near the model window); explicit values below 8000 are raised to 8000. Once the cap is reached after the agent's first run, the history is compacted to MARINA_AGENT_CONTEXT_TARGET_TOKENS (default a third of the cap) and kept; the originals are archived first. The near-window trigger still applies when it comes first. The built-in default exempts an agent bound to an active Code Mode task; an explicit value applies to every agent. |  |
| `MARINA_DROP_OLD_THINKING_SIGNATURES=on` | Removes reasoning blocks (text and provider signature) from assistant messages of earlier runs between prompts; the latest run is untouched, OpenAI Responses-API messages are skipped, and the originals stay in the continuity journal. On by default; `off` keeps every reasoning block. |  |
| `MARINA_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES=2` | Provider-level retries inside one request (transient 5xx, short 429) before the loop's own backoff. 0 disables. |  |
| `MARINA_PERCEIVE_SELF_ECHO=off` | `on` keeps an agent's own command echoes (memory-service acknowledgements, its `You tell …` receipts) in its world-event buffer. Off by default; messages from others are never filtered. |  |
| `MARINA_REFLECTOR_IDLE_STOP_MS=600000` | Stop a `reflect`-spawned memory reflector after this many idle milliseconds with no assistance job. 0 disables. |  |
| `MARINA_COGNITIVE_PROVENANCE=false` | `true` records full, payload-bearing cognitive provenance. Off by default. |  |

## Spend limits and failure breaker

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD=50` | Daily USD cap (UTC day, persisted) on everything this world pays upstream: /v1 passthru, agent turns, decision backends, forecasts and priced media jobs. At the cap /v1 returns 429 spend_cap_reached, decisions, forecasts and priced media jobs are refused and agents pause until 00:00 UTC. Default 50; 0 or off = no cap; an invalid value keeps the default. `readiness` shows today's spend. The total is shared by every process on the same database: command-line runs (`bun run futurex`, `forecast`, `arena`, `metaculus`, `forecastbench`, …) attach the DB_PATH ledger and are checked against the persisted day total, so each run does not get a fresh cap. A command-line run without a database counts per process and warns once. | protected |
| `MARINA_SPEND_SCOPE=futurex-live` | Optional budget scope for this process (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, `:`; at most 64; case-insensitive). Its spend is recorded under the scope as well as in the world total, and the process is refused when EITHER its scope cap OR MARINA_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD is reached, so a scope only narrows the budget. Use one scope per job, for example a live watcher and a backtest. An invalid name refuses all spend. `readiness` lists today's scopes. | protected |
| `MARINA_SPEND_SCOPE_CAP_USD=50` | The daily USD cap for MARINA_SPEND_SCOPE (UTC day, persisted). Default 50; 0 or off = no scope cap (the world cap still applies); an invalid value keeps the default. | protected |
| `MARINA_CHILD_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD=50` | Daily cap a World Collective child world starts with (default 50, never above the parent's cap; 0 or off = the parent's cap). | protected |
| `MARINA_MAX_COST_USD_PER_HOUR=5`<br>`MARINA_MAX_AGENT_COST_USD_PER_HOUR=1` | Rolling one-hour USD caps on agent model spend, across all agents and per agent. Unset or 0 is unlimited. At a cap the agent pauses, tells its spawner, and resumes once last-hour spend drops. Local models count as $0. | protected |
| `MARINA_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_UPSTREAM_ERRORS=20`<br>`MARINA_UPSTREAM_ERROR_PAUSE_MS=600000` | Consecutive upstream or loop errors (429, 5xx, timeouts) before an agent pauses for MARINA_UPSTREAM_ERROR_PAUSE_MS milliseconds and tells its spawner once. |  |

## Code Mode

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_CODE_ROOTS=/workspaces/project-a` | Comma-separated directories `code` sessions may operate in. With neither this nor MARINA_CODE_DEFAULT_ROOT set, the working directory is a read-only root and host edits and command execution are refused. `marina .` sets this for the folder it opens. | restart |
| `MARINA_CODE_DEFAULT_ROOT=` | Default root for new sessions (must be inside MARINA_CODE_ROOTS). Defaults to the first root; set alone it also enables host execution in that directory. | restart |
| `MARINA_CODE_EXEC_UNRESTRICTED=` | Comma-separated entity ids or names eligible for headless approval of arbitrary (non-allowlisted) host commands. Each also needs the code.exec.unrestricted gate unsupervised and a trusted identity on the acting connection (signed in, or loopback). Interactive approval (`code exec-mode prompt`) does not use this list. | protected |
| `MARINA_CODE_EXEC_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS=120000` | Interactive exec-approval prompt timeout in milliseconds. |  |
| `MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_RUNTIME=` | Container runtime for container-backed workspaces (`podman` or `docker`). Unset picks podman, then docker. With neither installed, a container runner refuses every command; it never falls back to host execution. |  |
| `MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_IMAGE=`<br>`MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_SYNC=mount`<br>`MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_WORKDIR=/work`<br>`MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_INIT=`<br>`MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_SHELL=sh`<br>`MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_NETWORK=off` | Operator container runner for local Code Mode sessions: finite commands (tests, scripts) run inside this image instead of on the host. Same allowlist, approvals and code.exec gate as host runs; no network unless MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_NETWORK is on; capabilities dropped; CPU/memory/pid limits. While MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_REQUIRED is in force (the default once IMAGE is set) this is policy: in-world `code workspace runner` cannot return to the host or change the image, runtime, sync, workdir, shell, network or init; sessions tune only cpus/memory/timeout. SYNC=mount (default) binds the worktree at WORKDIR (default /work) on a read-only root, with the repository's .git bound read-only (a root without its own .git is refused); SYNC=patch mounts nothing and applies the pending diff inside a throwaway container whose image already holds the project at WORKDIR. INIT is a one-line environment preamble (e.g. activating a conda env) run by SHELL (sh or bash); it is operator-only and never settable in-world. |  |
| `MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_REQUIRED=` | Whether local Code Mode sessions must run their commands in a container. Unset: required exactly when MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_IMAGE is set. `true`: required even without an image (sessions then pick one with `code workspace runner container image:<ref>`, which needs the code.exec.unrestricted gate; until then commands fail, never run on the host). `false`: the operator image is only a default and a session may choose `code workspace runner local`. Env-only; nothing in-world changes it. |  |
| `MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_STORAGE=`<br>`MARINA_CODE_CONTAINER_RUNROOT=` | Podman image store (`--root`) and runtime state (`--runroot`) for container workspaces, as absolute paths. Unset uses the operator's own Podman storage, resolved from the server's startup HOME / XDG_* / CONTAINERS_* environment (never the scratch HOME Code Mode gives host commands). Podman only; set Docker's data-root in the daemon. `code doctor` warns when the store is on tmpfs or under /tmp. |  |
| `MARINA_CODE_VERIFY_SCOPE=auto`<br>`MARINA_CODE_VERIFY_DEPENDENCIES=check`<br>`MARINA_CODE_VERIFY_TYPECHECK=auto`<br>`MARINA_CODE_VERIFY_FULL_BUDGET=10m` | Defaults for `code verify` (each overridable per call with the modifier of the same name). SCOPE: `auto` runs the tests relevant to the change (touched tests, tests named after touched files, tests that import them) and falls back to the full suite when none are found; `changed` runs only relevant tests (not_run when there are none); `full` runs the whole suite; `changed+full` runs relevant tests, then the full suite within FULL_BUDGET. DEPENDENCIES: `check` probes the environment for the detected project type and reports not_run when it is not ready; `none` skips the probe; `auto` (or the project's own manager) also installs locked dependencies where isolated (a candidate's Bun text lockfile without scripts, or a container runner with sync mount and network on). A manager for another language is never run. TYPECHECK: `auto` runs the project's configured tsc / mypy / pyright; `off` skips it. Invalid values fall back to the defaults. |  |

## Search

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `TAVILY_API_KEY=` | Web search upgrades. Search works with no key (DuckDuckGo plus arXiv, PubMed and Semantic Scholar); Tavily or a self-hosted SearXNG improves results. A backend that fails — a key out of credit (Tavily answers HTTP 432), an outage, the daily spend cap — falls through to the next (Tavily → SearXNG → DuckDuckGo), is named in the reply and shows in `readiness` (check `search`); Tavily calls are priced into the daily spend ledger (source `search`). The `search` research retriever uses the same backends (see MARINA_RESEARCH_SEARCH_BACKENDS). | secret, restart |
| `SEARXNG_URL=http://localhost:8080` | Web search upgrades. Search works with no key (DuckDuckGo plus arXiv, PubMed and Semantic Scholar); Tavily or a self-hosted SearXNG improves results. A backend that fails — a key out of credit (Tavily answers HTTP 432), an outage, the daily spend cap — falls through to the next (Tavily → SearXNG → DuckDuckGo), is named in the reply and shows in `readiness` (check `search`); Tavily calls are priced into the daily spend ledger (source `search`). The `search` research retriever uses the same backends (see MARINA_RESEARCH_SEARCH_BACKENDS). | restart |
| `MARINA_RESEARCH_SEARCH_BACKENDS=tavily,exa,searxng,duckduckgo,openrouter`<br>`MARINA_RESEARCH_SEARCH_MODEL=openai/gpt-6-luna`<br>`MARINA_RESEARCH_MAX_PASSAGES=15`<br>`MARINA_RESEARCH_RESULTS_PER_QUERY=8`<br>`MARINA_RESEARCH_DOMAIN_CAP=3`<br>`MARINA_RESEARCH_MAX_PAGES=14`<br>`MARINA_RESEARCH_PASSAGE_CHARS=` | The `search` research retriever (forecasts, typed answers, `MARINA_ARENA_RESEARCH_RETRIEVER=search`): every planned query goes through a backend chain, the pages are read (SSRF-guarded, never a no-fetch publisher) and the passages most relevant to the question are quoted verbatim, dated, so the citation check verifies them. BACKENDS is the chain in fallback order (tavily, exa, searxng, duckduckgo, openrouter; default: every configured one, then keyless duckduckgo, then — with OPENROUTER_API_KEY — OpenRouter's Exa web plugin as the paid fallback when DuckDuckGo throttles; SEARCH_MODEL is the model that carries that call); a backend that fails is skipped for the rest of the brief and reported. The question's named resolution page is read before any search. MAX_PASSAGES is the relevance top-k cut per brief (default 15; passages far below the best are dropped too). RESULTS_PER_QUERY (default 8), DOMAIN_CAP (pages per site, default 3, for source diversity) and MAX_PAGES (pages read per brief, default 14) set breadth; PASSAGE_CHARS fixes the passage budget per brief (default: the forecast's own evidence budget, sized to the model's context window). Paid backends check the daily spend cap and record their cost (source `search`). |  |
| `MARINA_CORPUS_DIR=~/.local/share/marina/corpora` | Where local corpora live: offline BM25 indexes built with `bun run corpus build <name> <docs.jsonl>` and searched with `web search engines:corpus:<name>`, the search room, or the `corpus:<name>` research retriever. Keep it on a disk with room (a 100k-document corpus is several GB), not a small temp filesystem. |  |
| `MARINA_CORPUS_RANKING=rescored`<br>`MARINA_CORPUS_BM25_K1=`<br>`MARINA_CORPUS_BM25_B=` | Corpus ranking. Each query's top 1,000 FTS5 candidates are rescored with BM25 k1 = 6, b = 1 (Porter-stemmed term counts, document length in characters): full length normalisation, which beat FTS5's built-in bm25() (k1 = 1.2, b = 0.75, tuned for short passages) on held-out query splits of a long-document corpus. Set BOTH K1 and B to rescore with other parameters; MARINA_CORPUS_RANKING=fts5 keeps FTS5's own ranking. Rankings are cached, so paging through results (`offset`) is cheap; a rescored search costs about 1–3 s on a 100k-document corpus (FTS5 alone ≈ 0.3 s). The BrowseComp-Plus harness ranks with FTS5 unless K1 and B are set explicitly. |  |
| `MARINA_CORPUS_EMBEDDINGS=none`<br>`MARINA_CORPUS_EMBEDDING_URL=`<br>`MARINA_CORPUS_EMBEDDING_MODEL=`<br>`MARINA_CORPUS_EMBEDDING_REVISION=` | Optional hybrid corpus search: the query embedder. none (default) keeps every corpus on BM25 exactly as above. local (the pinned MiniLM extension), ollama (an operator-run /api/embed) or openai (ANY OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings: OpenAI, OpenRouter, a local llama.cpp / vLLM / TEI server; URL, model and an operator-declared immutable revision required). Hybrid search applies only to a corpus holding vectors from the same model (`bun run corpus embed <name>` with this configuration, or `bun run corpus vectors import`); otherwise, and on any embedding failure or the daily spend cap, the search is BM25 and says so. Paid query embeddings are recorded in the spend ledger as `search`. The API key falls back to OPENROUTER_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY only for those vendors' own hosts. DIMENSIONS asks the server for a Matryoshka-truncated vector (the stored vectors must match). | protected |
| `MARINA_CORPUS_EMBEDDING_API_KEY=` | Optional hybrid corpus search: the query embedder. none (default) keeps every corpus on BM25 exactly as above. local (the pinned MiniLM extension), ollama (an operator-run /api/embed) or openai (ANY OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings: OpenAI, OpenRouter, a local llama.cpp / vLLM / TEI server; URL, model and an operator-declared immutable revision required). Hybrid search applies only to a corpus holding vectors from the same model (`bun run corpus embed <name>` with this configuration, or `bun run corpus vectors import`); otherwise, and on any embedding failure or the daily spend cap, the search is BM25 and says so. Paid query embeddings are recorded in the spend ledger as `search`. The API key falls back to OPENROUTER_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY only for those vendors' own hosts. DIMENSIONS asks the server for a Matryoshka-truncated vector (the stored vectors must match). | secret, protected |

## Model routing

With neither tiers nor MARINA_ROUTES set, model:route has one candidate (this installation's first available model, else marina/default) and says so in the route event; with tiers but no backend or goal, the powerful tier is used. |  |

Low confidence (&lt; 0.6), no backend or an error use MARINA_ROUTE_FALLBACK (default `powerful` if present, else the last route). |  |
| `MARINA_ROUTE_EVIDENCE=off`<br>`MARINA_ROUTE_EVIDENCE_FAMILIES=hle-verified-gold,frames`<br>`MARINA_ROUTE_EVIDENCE_MIN_N=30`<br>`MARINA_ROUTE_EVIDENCE_MAX_COST_USD=0.05`<br>`MARINA_ROUTE_EVIDENCE_WINDOW=false` | Benchmark evidence for model:route (src/engine/benchmark-evidence.ts). After the router picks, measured ledger results may prefer another of the SAME candidates: the best Wilson lower bound among at least two candidates with MIN_N items in the role's families (and within MAX_COST_USD per item, when set). `observe` records the pick on the route decision without acting; `on` applies it. Resolved once at spawn and persisted; any error keeps the router's choice. Families: a comma list of benchmark names for every role, or JSON {"*": [...], "&lt;role&gt;": [...]}; with none, evidence never applies. Evidence is traced participants and direct-model runs; window evidence only with MARINA_ROUTE_EVIDENCE_WINDOW=true, shared window evidence never. Inspect with `trace advise evidence <benchmark>`. |  |
| `MARINA_ROUTE_EVIDENCE_OBJECTIVE=lcb`<br>`MARINA_ROUTE_EVIDENCE_TOLERANCE=0.05` | What the evidence pick optimizes. - `lcb` (default): the best Wilson lower bound. - `budget`: the best lower bound within MARINA_ROUTE_EVIDENCE_MAX_COST_USD per item; it never picks without a budget. - `value`: the CHEAPEST priced candidate not measurably worse than the best-lower-bound one. Its point accuracy must be within TOLERANCE (absolute, 0–1) of the best's. With at least MIN_N shared items, a paired exact McNemar test must not show a significant loss (p &lt; 0.05); otherwise its interval must overlap the best's lower bound. Evidence is per role first (participants whose agent plays the spawning role) and falls back to model level when fewer than two candidates have MIN_N role items. |  |
| `MARINA_PROMOTION_MIN_REPLICATES=2` | Replicates a challenger needs before `benchmark promote` reads a slot's holdout (src/engine/benchmark-promotion.ts). A replicate is another ledger run of the same target on the same items with the same judge (one replicate group). With replicates on either side, the paired interval is a two-stage bootstrap (runs, then items), so run-to-run variance counts against the gain. An integer from 1 to 100; 1 restores single-run promotion. Anything else is the default. |  |
| `MARINA_BENCHMARK_MAX_FALLBACK_RATE=0.25` | Share of a benchmark run's items that may be fallbacks — an error, a spend-cap or provider refusal, or an unparseable reply replaced by a default — before the ledger records the run `invalid` (src/engine/benchmark-ledger.ts). An invalid run keeps its items but is excluded from every ledger reader (leaderboard, frontier, compare, replicates, participants, promotion, route evidence); `benchmark runs` and `benchmark result` show it marked with the reason, and `benchmark revalidate` (role.edit) reverses it. Read wherever a run is recorded: the server (in-world runs and POST /v1/benchmarks/runs), `bun run benchmark:import` and `bun run futurex`. A share from 0 to 1, exceeded strictly; `off` (or 1) disables the check; junk is the default. The default is conservative: a few timeouts are the target's own failures and stay scored. |  |

## Forecasting

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_FORECAST_ANALYSTS=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro,openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5,openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_RETRIEVER=openrouter-web:openai/gpt-6-luna@exa,search`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_JUDGE=jev` | `forecast`, `bun run forecast` and POST /v1/forecast (docs/guides/forecasting.md). No vendor key is required: unset, every part sizes to what is configured (docs/guides/single-model.md). Analysts are a comma list of models (defaults: DeepSeek V4 Pro, Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-6 Luna via OpenRouter; without OPENROUTER_API_KEY, the configured providers or a single local model, which then answers as the one analyst × K runs); the retriever defaults to OpenRouter web search on GPT-6 Luna over Exa plus the `search` retriever (every planned query through the search backend chain, pages read and quoted), else `search` alone (keyless DuckDuckGo when no search key is set); the judge is jev (without OPENROUTER_API_KEY: the MARINA_DECISIONS backend, else no judge), decisions (the MARINA_DECISIONS backend, falling back to jev) or none. Substitutions are reported as the answer's `scale` (tier `degraded`); only having no model at all is an error. |  |
| `MARINA_FORECAST_DOSSIER_CHARS=`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_FOLLOWUP=on`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_MIN_EVIDENCE=5`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_DISAGREEMENT=on` | Evidence depth for typed forecasts. DOSSIER_CHARS is the research dossier each run reads (default: sized to the analysts' context window, 12 000–60 000 characters; 24 000 when unknown); when the dossier is longer, verified lines are kept first. MIN_EVIDENCE is the number of verified lines wanted before the runs (default 5; 0 = off): fewer triggers one more research round first. Otherwise FOLLOWUP=on (default) runs that one extra round after the runs when none is grounded in verified evidence, and redoes the runs only if it verified something new; off disables both. DISAGREEMENT=on (default): when the runs disagree (agreement below 0.7), one round searches the point they disagree on and one more run reads it, pooled with the others. |  |
| `MARINA_FORECAST_PLANNER=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_CRITIC=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_RUNS=3`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_RESEARCH_ROUNDS=2`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_CRITIQUE=on`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_LOOKUPS=auto` | Typed forecasts (a choice, a set of options, a number, a ranking or a short string; `forecast … type:<t>`, `bun run forecast --type`, POST /v1/forecast with `answer`). The retriever also accepts openrouter-web:&lt;model&gt;@exa\|@native (the web plugin's engine; Exa excerpts serve the citation check), sonar:&lt;model&gt;, tavily:&lt;basic\|advanced&gt; (TAVILY_API_KEY), search[:&lt;backend&gt;+&lt;backend&gt;…] and asof[:&lt;providers&gt;] (keyless and date-strict, bounded to each forecast's cutoff: gdelt, wikipedia, hn, arxiv, wayback; docs/guides/search.md), comma-separated to merge. The planner decomposes the question and names research gaps (default: the first analyst); the critic searches for evidence against the leading answer and may revise it only when its confidence exceeds the runs' agreement (default: the planner). RUNS independent answers (1–9, analysts used round-robin) are combined by type; RESEARCH_ROUNDS bounds the search loop (1–4); CRITIQUE=off skips the disconfirmation pass. LOOKUPS picks structured sources (also answerable directly with the `data` command): unset or `auto` (the default) turns on every one that can run here — polymarket, kalshi, fred and bls (keyless) plus odds when ODDS_API_KEY is set; `off` or `none` (or empty) turns them off; otherwise a comma list: polymarket and kalshi (market prices; a past cutoff reads the last price at or before it, never the resolution), odds (sports head-to-head odds via ODDS_API_KEY; historical snapshots need a paid plan), fred (official series; vintage-correct for a past cutoff with FRED_API_KEY, live-only without), bls (live-only), or markets / all. Every lookup reads as of the earlier of the cutoff and now. A number is anchored on the freshest official reading with a horizon-scaled spread. |  |
| `MARINA_FORECAST_FORMATION=ensemble` | How POST /v1/forecast combines a typed forecast's runs (src/forecast/formations.ts): `ensemble` (default — combined by type, then the critique), `delphi` (each member revises once after an anonymous panel summary; median of the revisions), `tournament` (pairwise knockout judged by the critic; the champion's answer) or `skeptic` (the arena's crew: the first two analysts propose as statistician and analyst, the critic — else the third analyst — sets how much of their move away from the prior to trust; deterministic aggregation that only shrinks toward an informative prior — never the uniform default; without one the proposals' log-odds mean stands; one model runs every role). The research and cutoff are the same for all of them. |  |
| `MARINA_FORECAST_PRIOR=off`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_PRIOR_WEIGHT=0.5`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_CALIBRATION=off`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_CALIBRATION_MARGIN=0.05`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_CALIBRATION_SCORE=brier`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_PROB_CLAMP=0.01`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_POOL=linear`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_HISTORY=data/forecast/history.jsonl`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_HISTORY_MIN=50` | Prior shrink and recalibration for typed forecasts (src/forecast/adjust.ts), both off by default and applied once at the end of any formation. PRIOR=on pools the finished answer toward the best prior available at the evidence cutoff — a market or community forecast the caller supplied (`priors` on POST /v1/forecast), one priced market a lookup matched for a yes/no question, the freshest official reading for a number, the question class's base rate in resolved history, else the type default — in log-odds (numbers: linearly). PRIOR_WEIGHT (0–1, default 0.5) is the weight toward a supplied market or community prior before there is evidence; every other prior starts at 0. Only an INFORMATIVE prior earns a shrink (never the uniform type default, which would only add to the hedging LLM forecasters show); with enough records in a time-to-close bucket (≤ 7 d, ≤ 30 d, &gt; 30 d; and liquidity below/above $10k when the caller supplies `liquidity`) the weight is fitted there, so a liquid market near its close can earn more weight than a thin one far from it. CALIBRATION=on applies a recalibration map per answer group (Platt in log-odds for choices and multi-selects, an sd scale for numbers); `observe` fits and records it without applying it; `fixed:<a>` (e.g. `fixed:sqrt3`, 0.25–4) applies a fixed Platt slope from the first forecast with no history — the cold start for a new board (a &gt; 1 extremizes). PROB_CLAMP (0.0001–0.2) holds final probabilities inside [ε, 1 − ε], a tail guard for log-scored boards. POOL=logodds averages the runs' probabilities in log-odds (a geometric pool) instead of arithmetically (`linear`, the default). A learned weight or map is fitted on the older 60 % of the resolved history visible at the cutoff and replaces its default only when it improves CALIBRATION_SCORE (`brier` or `log`; numbers use CRPS) on the newer 40 % by at least CALIBRATION_MARGIN (relative, default 0.05) — and only with at least HISTORY_MIN visible records (default 50). HISTORY is a JSON-lines file of resolved forecasts (numbers and option ids only, no question text) that adapters append to as questions resolve; a record is used only when its outcome was known at the forecast's cutoff, and never for its own question. Every prior, weight and map is recorded on the answer (`adjustment`). |  |
| `MARINA_FORECAST_ROUTE=off`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_ROUTE_CANDIDATES=ensemble,delphi,tournament,skeptic`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_ROUTE_MIN_N=30` | Formation routing for POST /v1/forecast (src/forecast/routing.ts): `off` (default) answers with MARINA_FORECAST_FORMATION; `observe` records which formation routing would pick; `on` uses it. Per question class (the caller's `category`, else the answer group) a challenger replaces the default only when, on at least ROUTE_MIN_N questions both answered (resolved records in MARINA_FORECAST_HISTORY carrying their formation and score), its paired gain has a 95 % lower bound above 0 and clears the fishing margin 0.02 + 0.01·log₂(1 + challengers tried). CANDIDATES is a comma list of formations (default all four). |  |
| `MARINA_FORECAST_VERIFY=off`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_VERIFIER=`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_RETRIEVAL_FILTER=none` | Verification inside a typed forecast: with VERIFY=on each run's draft is checked by VERIFIER (default: the critic) against the dossier and the resolution rules before it is combined, and a concrete correction replaces it. RETRIEVAL_FILTER=strict keeps only research lines whose every cited page is provably published on or before the evidence cutoff (engine date, else a date in the URL) and that name no later day; undated and live-result pages are dropped. Use it for past-cutoff forecasts (replays, backtests); date-filtered engines (tavily:, exa:) need no filter, and `closed-book` as the retriever disables retrieval. |  |
| `MARINA_FORECAST_BUDGET_S=0` | Wall-clock budget per typed forecast, in seconds (unset or 0 = none). Budget-terminal answering: from about 75 % no further research round starts; at the cap lookups, verification and the critique are skipped and the answer is combined from the runs finished so far (the first run to finish, when none has). The answer then carries `budgetForced`, and a skipped check is recorded as `not_run`, never as a failure. |  |
| `MARINA_FORECAST_SELECTION=agreement` | How a typed forecast's K runs become one answer. `agreement` (the default) combines the runs by type and reports their agreement as the confidence. `confidence` takes the run with the highest self-reported confidence and reports that confidence, which is the bar a critique must clear to replace it. Agreement among same-model runs measures consistency, not correctness. The default changes only after `confidence` wins on a held-out split by the promotion margin (`benchmarks/futurex/rescore-selection.ts` re-scores saved forecasts offline). |  |
| `EXA_API_KEY=` | Exa search for forecast and arena retrieval (`exa:auto`, `exa:neural`, `exa:keyword`): filtered server-side by publication date to the brief's window, so it is a date-filtered engine. | secret, restart |
| `ODDS_API_KEY=`<br>`FRED_API_KEY=`<br>`BLS_API_KEY=` | Keys for forecast lookups (each lookup is skipped when its key is unset): The Odds API (sports odds), FRED (St. Louis Fed; vintage data for a past cutoff), and BLS (optional; raises the public API's quota). | secret, protected |
| `MARINA_FORECAST_MARINA_URL=http://localhost:3300`<br>`MARINA_FORECAST_MARINA_KEY=` | An analyst written `marina:<crew>` asks that crew through a Marina server's model API (for example a crew in the verification formation). URL defaults to http://localhost:3300; the key is that server's MODEL_API_KEYS entry. The crew's spend is recorded by that server. | protected |

| `MARINA_VERIFY_CHECKER_EFFORT=inherit` | `marina/verify:` checker reasoning effort. `inherit` copies the caller's own effort (`reasoning_effort`, `reasoning`, `thinking`, top level or inside a literal `extra_body`); `low`/`medium`/`high` send that `reasoning_effort`; `off` sends none (the checker model's default, no thinking for Claude). The upstream layer translates it per provider. Default inherit. |  |
| `MARINA_VISION_MODEL=openrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol` | Vision model for `canvas look` / `image describe` / `video describe` / `marina_see` when the agent's own model cannot read images. Unset: the agent's model, else Marina's default route. |  |
| `MARINA_VISION_MAX_BYTES=20971520` | Byte cap on an image, PDF, video or text a vision call will load (max 100 MB). Default 20 MB. |  |
| `MARINA_COMPAT=openai` | Comma-separated drop-in compatibility profiles whose model-id aliases appear in /v1/models (`openai` exposes `assistant`). Default all; `none` disables. |  |

## HTTP hardening

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES=8388608`<br>`MARINA_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES=52428800` | Request body ceiling for JSON routes (enforced per route; pre-auth and key-management routes use a 64 KiB cap), and the separate cap on one asset upload (uploads are MIME-allowlisted and magic-byte checked). | restart |
| `MARINA_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS=300000` | Deadline in milliseconds for one proxied upstream model call (response headers for a stream, the whole reply otherwise). A non-streaming call is also aborted when its client disconnects. |  |
| `MARINA_MCP_SESSIONS_PER_MIN=10` | MCP session creations and login/auth tool calls per client IP per minute. 0 disables. |  |
| `MARINA_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=mcp.example.com` | Extra Host header values /mcp accepts (DNS-rebinding protection; validation is never off). Unset on a non-loopback bind: only loopback names, a specific bind address, the machine hostname and the BETTER_AUTH_URL / ALLOWED_ORIGINS hosts. List LAN IPs or other names clients use here. | protected |
| `MARINA_URL_GUARD_DNS_FAIL_OPEN=false` | `true` lets outbound fetches proceed when DNS resolution fails, instead of refusing them (fail open). Only for restricted-DNS environments. | protected |

## Retention

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_RETENTION_OVERRIDES=primitive_usage=30d,feed_events=0` | Override row-retention windows: comma-separated table=&lt;duration\|rows\|0&gt;, durations in s/m/h/d/w, a bare integer is a row count, 0 never prunes. Per-class defaults and the table list live in src/engine/retention.ts (Admin → Ops shows them); append-only tables can never be pruned. |  |
| `MARINA_EVENT_RETENTION=100000` | Durable event_log rows kept (pruned hourly; clamped 10000–10000000). |  |
| `MARINA_LOG_RETENTION=10000` | Structured application log rows kept in SQLite (maximum 1000000). | restart |

## Logging and OpenTelemetry

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `LOG_FORMAT=text`<br>`LOG_LEVEL=info` | Log format (text or json) and minimum level (debug, info, warn, error; case-insensitive — an invalid level warns once and uses info). | restart |
| `MARINA_OTLP_ENABLED=false` | `true` pushes completed structural spans to an OTLP/HTTP JSON collector. Prompts, outputs, tool arguments and credentials are excluded; a collector outage never blocks agents. | restart |
| `MARINA_OTLP_LOGS_ENABLED=false` | `true` pushes logs over OTLP/HTTP JSON, independently of traces. | restart |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://collector.example` | Shared OTLP base endpoint (Marina appends /v1/traces or /v1/logs), headers (comma-separated, percent-encoded key=value, never displayed), timeout (default 10s, clamped 100ms–60s) and protocol (only http/json is supported). Each has a per-signal OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_* or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_* variant that wins; per-signal endpoints are used exactly as written. | restart |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=` | Shared OTLP base endpoint (Marina appends /v1/traces or /v1/logs), headers (comma-separated, percent-encoded key=value, never displayed), timeout (default 10s, clamped 100ms–60s) and protocol (only http/json is supported). | Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|

## Command-line clients

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_URL=ws://localhost:3300` | Server URL for `marina connect`, `marina status`, the ACP bridge (scripts/acp.ts) and the routing CLIs. Read by those clients, not the server. | internal |
| `MARINA_TOKEN=` | Bearer token `marina status` and the routing CLIs send. Unset reuses the newest cached `marina connect` session for MARINA_URL. | secret, internal |
| `MARINA_CODE_FRESH=`<br>`MARINA_CODE_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS=600000` | Folder launcher (`marina [dir]`, `bun run code`): `1` uses a throwaway database deleted on exit (same as --fresh) instead of ~/.marina/projects/&lt;slug&gt;/marina.db, and the one-shot `marina -p` timeout in milliseconds (on timeout it sends `code stop` and exits 2). | internal |

## Set by Marina (do not set)

| Variable | Description | Flags |
|---|---|---|
| `MARINA_LOCAL_API_KEY=` | The local profile's generated model-API key, loaded from &lt;DB_PATH&gt;.local-api-key at boot; ignored and dropped under shared/public. It also opens /mem with an X-Agent-Name header. Do not set it yourself. | secret, protected, internal |
| `MARINA_COLLECTIVE_CHILD=` | Marks a World Collective child world, which lets `evolve trial` run there. Set by the collective manager; setting it on a parent world bypasses the trial fence. | protected, internal |
